text: The Museum of Recent Art (Romanian: Muzeul de Artă Recentă, or MARe) is a contemporary art museum situated in Bucharest, Romania, within the Primăverii district. Its collection includes over 1,000 artworks by more than 250 Romanian and international artists, spanning more than 150 pieces displayed across a five-level, 1,200 square meter facility. The term "recent" primarily denotes the temporal scope of the collection, covering Romanian art from the post-Stalinist period to the present, with international art featured through temporary exhibitions. The museum is designed to be more open and accessible than traditional Romanian museums, offering a library and other cultural spaces for the community. The building was constructed on the site of an interwar villa that previously stood in the area, which had architectural influences from Western (Moorish) design. This villa was demolished, and the museum's guided tours incorporate its historical narrative, including the fact that Ana Pauker, a prominent Communist Party leader during the proletkultist era, once lived there. There are also references to underground tunnels beneath the villa, contributing to its historical significance. The architectural design, by Youssef Tohme Architects & Associates, features a unified monolithic structure made of dark-colored brick resting on a fully glazed space, creating a large, open atrium facing the street. Notable artists represented in the collection include Ion Țuculescu, Andrei Cădere, Horia Bernea, Ion Grigorescu, Dan Perjovschi, Hermann Nitsch, Lucio Fontana, and Michelangelo Pistoletto.
